text: I call company, walking, riding, etc., employing one's time, and, upon proper occasions, very usefully; but what I cannot forgive in anybody is sauntering, and doing nothing at all, with a thing so precious as time, and so irrecoverable when lost.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter IV, to his son, London, December 9, Old Style 1746
